correctness.summary: Lassak's butterfly-area bound reduces the problem to a Jensen deficit for an explicit concave function. Monotonicity of -f'' gives asymmetric quadratic tangent-deficit bounds; the zero-sum angle constraint combines them into the stated coefficient. A limiting angle vector supplies the matching first two asymptotic terms for the best scalar coefficient.

limitations: The theorem controls canonical angles rather than Hausdorff or vertex-coordinate distance.
The explicit polygon coefficient is not claimed globally optimal over realizable reduced polygons.
Two-term optimality is for the underlying angle-simplex inequality, not for the full geometric area deficit.
Originality remains subject to residual risk from unindexed, inaccessible, or differently phrased literature.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The 2005 source gives qualitative strict extremality via Jensen. Searches of later reduced-body surveys, recent reduced-polygon work, exact terminology, and the scalar formula found no quantitative canonical-angle variance refinement or matching two-term stability constant.

review_statement: Same-model review: passed. Independent audit: not yet performed.

value.summary: The result turns qualitative maximality of the regular reduced n-gon into an explicit inverse stability theorem and identifies the asymptotically optimal first two terms of the scalar Jensen-stability scale.
